A ground-up, full-semester course that builds the modern deep-learning stack — from the probability under every loss, through CNNs and Transformers, to LLMs and diffusion.

::: {.callout-tip}

Lecture decks, runnable notebooks, and assignments live on the **[course materials site ↗](https://nipunbatra.github.io/dl-teaching/)**. This page is just the logistics: [schedule](schedule.qmd), [grading](grading.qmd), [deadlines](deadlines.qmd), and [FAQ](faq.qmd).
:::

## Communication

Announcements, deadlines, and questions live in the **[ES 667 Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/dl26workspace/shared_invite/zt-43b3v79vb-bVZl1_sJVCrBkVMDsq5TYA)** — join before the first week.

## What you'll learn

Foundations (losses, backprop) → optimization & regularization → CNNs → sequences & Transformers → representation & multimodal learning → generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion) → efficient systems. The full module map and lecture list is on the [materials site](https://nipunbatra.github.io/dl-teaching/slides.html); assessment is **three programming assignments** and **quizzes** (see [Grading](grading.qmd)).

## Textbooks

No book is required; these three carry most of the course, all free online:

1. **Understanding Deep Learning** — Prince, MIT Press 2023 · [free](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/)
2. **Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts** — Bishop & Bishop, Springer 2024
3. **Dive into Deep Learning** — Zhang, Lipton, Li & Smola · [free](https://d2l.ai/)

A fuller reading list is on the materials site's [Resources](https://nipunbatra.github.io/dl-teaching/resources.html) page.
